data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A halted run is resumable without corrupting append-only identity iff three conditions hold simultaneously: (1) the halt occurred at an event boundary, meaning the last event in the log was fully written and its identity digest (hash-chain link) is finalized and persisted; (2) the persisted token-budget state is consistent with the event-log position\u2014every event's token cost has been accounted for and the remaining budget is exactly what it would be after replaying all committed events; (3) the system's continuation is a pure function of the persisted event log plus budget state, with no un-logged non-deterministic inputs (external tool-call results, RNG draws, real-world side effects) that would alter the next event's content. Resumption must be refused whenever any of these fails: a torn/partial tail event, a budget-state mismatch, a broken hash chain, or reliance on volatile external state not captured in the log.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The tail event is partially written (torn write): the persisted bytes do not form a complete event with a valid digest, so the chain has no finalized link target for the next event.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Budget state and event log are inconsistent: e.g., budget was decremented for an event that failed to persist, or an event persisted without budget decrement, so the resumed run's resource decisions diverge from a continuous run.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The hash chain is broken at any point: a gap, a reordering, or a corrupted intermediate event makes the append-only identity already invalid before resumption.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The run consumed non-deterministic external inputs (tool calls, RNG, real-world state) whose outputs are not fully recorded in committed events, so the resumed run cannot reconstruct the exact continuation trajectory.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Volatile generation state (e.g., KV cache contents, attention state) that influences event content is not derivable from the event log alone, and the system cannot deterministically reconstruct it.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Append-only identity is a hash chain (or equivalent digest structure) over the event sequence. Identity preservation requires that the chain be unbroken at the resumption point and that each new event links to the correct predecessor. A clean halt at an event boundary guarantees the predecessor is finalized. Budget consistency ensures the resumed run operates under the same resource constraints a continuous run would have had, so it produces the same sequence of decisions. Pure-function dependence on the log ensures the resumed events are causally consistent with the committed prefix\u2014no divergence from an uninterrupted run. If any condition fails, appending new events would either link to a corrupted/incomplete predecessor or produce events whose content diverges from what the original run trajectory would have generated, corrupting the identity in the sense that the chain no longer represents a single coherent run.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
